title: Lesson 30: Capstone: Run Your Own Engagement End to End
description: Run a full engagement from discovery through handover: the complete arc, the seams between phases, and how each prior lesson connects so you can carry an engagement to a clean close without a safety net.

questions.question: In the capstone lesson, what is the primary reason an engagement most often fails?
options: A phase is done badly in the middle because the consultant lacks a single technique
The consultant can only do each phase in isolation and cannot connect the phases at the seams
The client always changes the scope in bad faith
The tool cannot handle the client's workload
questions.explanation: The lesson says an engagement that fails usually fails not because any one technique was weak but because the consultant could only do one phase in isolation and could not connect discovery to design to handover when each phase stopped being scaffolded by a course.

questions.question: What does the lesson identify as the fix for a scope that has inclusions but excludes nothing?
options: Adding more inclusions until the client is satisfied
Writing exclusions plainly, because exclusions, not inclusions, are what stop scope creep
Lowering the price to discourage new requests
Waiting until the client asks for less work
questions.explanation: The lesson says a scope with only inclusions cannot stop scope creep because every new request is part of the problem, and the fix is written exclusions, since saying no in the contract is how you stay on time and on budget.

questions.question: Which statement best matches the lesson's guidance on guardrails?
options: Guardrails should be added after implementation as a cleanup step
Guardrails are a liability and should be avoided entirely
Guardrails are set during scoping and implemented as part of the build, before anything is built
Guardrails should only apply to irreversible actions
questions.explanation: The lesson says guardrails are set in the scoping step and implemented as part of the build, and that adding them after implementation means retrofitting safety onto an unconstrained system.
